baseline.license_note: Public open-source specification (not paywalled); short normative excerpts quoted below under fair use, full text not reproduced.
baseline.name: DSSE (Dead Simple Signing Envelope) Specification

claim_second_half_check.check: Do this module's checked-in docs (mission.md, capability-profile.json, shipped KPI) name the DSSE spec, PAE, or secure-systems-lab by name anywhere, i.e. is the divergence found here already 'deliberate and stated' against this specific named baseline?
claim_second_half_check.finding: mission.md uses the literal word 'DSSE' twice (both referring to the portfolio's OWN receipt-signing corpus / T-04's cross-check against amphora_core::verify_dsse), and no checked-in doc for this module ever cites the DSSE ENVELOPE SCHEMA or the PAE CONSTRUCTION as a named specification this predicate's own receipt format was measured against or deliberately diverges from. T-04 (2026-08-05) already established the BEHAVIORAL consequence (forged envelopes admitted); this run is the first to name the SPECIFICATION itself, pin its version, and show the receipt wire-format is structurally incompatible with the DSSE envelope schema independent of any particular forgery.

claim_under_attack.claim_text: The validator conforms to the published DSSE specification, and any divergence is deliberate and stated.

host_verified_receipt_schema_constructio.note: No production (non-#[cfg(test)]) code path in this file constructs a HOST_VERIFIED_RECEIPT_FEATURE value from a real amphora_core::verify_dsse() call; the only construction site(s) found are inside `mod tests` (starts line 1287).

requirements.evidence: Live host_receipt_valid (amphora-assurance-capabilities/src/lib.rs:729) checks a receipt object with cardinality 11 and fields ['accepted', 'candidate_id', 'fresh', 'package_sha256', 'revocation_checked', 'schema', 'signature_algorithm', 'signature_verified', 'trust_store_status']. None of payload/payloadType/signatures is present: {'payload': False, 'payloadType': False, 'signatures': False}.
requirements.normative_statement: The envelope MUST be a JSON object with exactly three top-level fields: payload, payloadType, and signatures (a required array).

requirements.evidence: No `payload` field exists anywhere in the checked receipt schema (11 fields, ['accepted', 'candidate_id', 'fresh', 'package_sha256', 'revocation_checked', 'schema', 'signature_algorithm', 'signature_verified', 'trust_store_status']); the signed-content analogue `package_sha256` is a SHA-256 digest, not a base64 body, so the actual bytes claimed to be signed are never carried through this validation boundary.
requirements.normative_statement: payload MUST be the Base64 encoding of the raw signed message bytes (SERIALIZED_BODY).

requirements.evidence: No `signatures` array or `keyid` field exists in the live receipt schema for this optionality rule to apply to.
requirements.normative_statement: signature.keyid is OPTIONAL; a verifier MUST NOT require or reject solely for its absence.
requirements.spec_citation: envelope.md :: "The following fields are OPTIONAL and MAY be unset: signature.keyid."

requirements.evidence: No `sig` field or signature object exists. The nearest field, `verifier_id`, is checked only via `.and_then(Value::as_str).is_some_and(|v| !v.is_empty())` -- a free-form non-empty string, not a decoded cryptographic signature.
requirements.normative_statement: Each entry in signatures MUST carry a `sig` field (the base64-encoded raw signature bytes).

requirements.evidence: The receipt schema is a flat JSON object (cardinality 11), not an array-bearing envelope; multi-signer / (t,n)-threshold trust is structurally impossible to express.
requirements.normative_statement: signatures MUST be an array, supporting zero or more independent signers over one payload.
requirements.spec_citation: envelope.md :: "An envelope MAY have more than one signature."

requirements.evidence: grep of the live evidence-intake region (lines 673-761) for the literal 'DSSEv1' token or a local `fn pae(` finds: False. Zero PAE computation of any kind occurs in this code path.
requirements.normative_statement: The signature MUST be computed, and MUST be verified, over the Pre-Authentication Encoding of (payloadType, body) -- never over the raw JSON envelope or the base64 payload string.
requirements.spec_citation: protocol.md :: PAE(type, body) = "DSSEv1" + SP + LEN(type) + SP + type + SP + LEN(body) + SP + body

requirements.evidence: host_receipt_valid calls verify_dsse: False; calls sign_dsse: False. The predicate instead performs `receipt.get("signature_verified").and_then(Value::as_bool) == Some(true)` -- a boolean-equality check on a value supplied by the caller's own FeatureSnapshot, not a value the module computes. Corroborated by T-04 (evidence/phase0/repairs/T-04/done/t04-adversarial-forgery-done.v1.dsse.json, 2026-08-05): 7/7 forged-DSSE-envelope cases across all 5 named forgery classes were ADMITTED by this predicate while `amphora_core::verify_dsse` correctly rejected the identical forged envelopes.
requirements.normative_statement: The verifier MUST itself decode SERIALIZED_BODY/PAYLOAD_TYPE/SIGNATURE and cryptographically verify SIGNATURE against the recomputed PAE; acceptance MUST be grounded in that computation, not in an externally supplied claim of having been verified.
requirements.spec_citation: protocol.md :: Verification procedure steps 1 and 3 ("Verify SIGNATURE against PAE(...). Reject if the verification fails")

requirements.evidence: No base64-encoded or PAE-structured field is present in the receipt schema for a decode step to apply to; the closest checks are JSON type/string-equality tests on already-parsed Value::as_str/as_bool.
requirements.normative_statement: The verifier MUST reject the envelope if base64/PAE decoding of any field fails.
requirements.spec_citation: protocol.md :: Verification procedure step 1 ("Reject if decoding fails")

requirements.evidence: Trust is granted on a single string-equality test `receipt.get("trust_store_status").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("TRUSTED")` with no ACCEPTED_KEYS set, no per-signature loop, and no independent trust-store lookup performed by this module -- the value is asserted by the caller-supplied FeatureSnapshot, exactly the pattern V1-REAL-EIV (2026-08-04) showed cannot be honestly reproduced from the repo's own config/phase0-trust-store.v1.json (0/66 real receipts anchor).
requirements.normative_statement: Any trust decision involving multiple/threshold signers MUST count only signatures whose cryptographic verification independently succeeded, not a self-reported trust flag.
requirements.spec_citation: protocol.md :: Multi-signature (t,n) verification ("add successful keys to ACCEPTED_KEYS... reject if the unique keys in ACCEPTED_KEYS is less than t")

requirements.evidence: No payload bytes are ever carried through this validation boundary (see R2), so there is no verified-vs-consumed byte pair for this guarantee to hold or violate; it is vacuously inapplicable rather than satisfied.
requirements.normative_statement: The bytes cryptographically verified MUST be the same bytes the application subsequently consumes (non-detachment guarantee).
requirements.spec_citation: envelope.md :: "Implementations MUST ensure that the same payload bytes that are verified are the ones sent to the application layer."

requirements.evidence: amphora-core/src/crypto.rs defines DsseEnvelope{payload_type, payload, signatures} (present: True), a PAE builder matching the spec formula (present: True), and verify_dsse() that decodes payload as base64 and verifies each signatures[] entry against the recomputed PAE. It is called 1 time(s) (sign) / 1 time(s) (verify) elsewhere in the SAME file (lines [299, 320]), by the sibling CroProtocolPackage capability, but zero times inside evaluate_evidence_intake/host_receipt_valid.
requirements.normative_statement: cross-check: does this codebase already ship a spec-conformant DSSE implementation that COULD have been used here?
requirements.spec_citation: protocol.md + envelope.md :: cross-check (not itself a MUST/SHOULD clause): PAE formula + envelope schema
